Slice: Send Overdue Notice

Intent

Tell a borrower by email that their loan is overdue, once per loan, so they return the tool. The shed records that the notice was handed to the email provider. That record shows the borrower was told, and stops a second notice.

Trigger & Actor

  • Trigger form: internally triggered. The Overdue Notice Gateway, a translation to the email provider outside the shed, watches the Overdue Loans To Notify list (slices/overdue-loans-to- notify.md). No person sends notices; only the gateway issues Send Overdue Notice.
  • When it reads: the list fills when midnight passes in the shed's local time, not when an event arrives, so the gateway reads it every 5 minutes, at any hour. A loan is therefore noticed within 5 minutes of becoming overdue (INV-OVN-6).
  • What the gateway does, for each loan on the list:
    1. It issues Send Overdue Notice for the loan, with the content from the loan's item: borrowerEmail, borrowerName, toolName and dueDate. If the command is refused, or is a repeat, nothing is sent for that loan.
    2. Each recorded Overdue Notice Sent is handed to the provider from the event itself, using the loan ID as the hand-off's key. The hand-off is driven by the recorded event, not by the list: if the hand-off call errors, or the process stops before the provider accepts, it is repeated with the same key (after a restart too) until the provider accepts it. This is an outbox, not a domain event.
  • The email: to the address recorded on the event, giving the borrower's name, the tool's name and the due date recorded on it, asking them to return the tool, and saying that an overdue loan blocks new checkouts and pickups (INV-OVN-3, INV-OVN-7).
  • The email port's contract, from the shed's house rules: the provider accepts a hand-off with a key, sends at most one email per key, makes its own delivery attempts (3 over about an hour), and sends one final failure report quoting the key, signed so the shed can trust it. The final failure is recorded by Record Overdue Notice Failure (slices/record-overdue-notice- failure.md).

Command / Input

Command: Send Overdue Notice

A LoanId is a UUID. "Today" is the calendar date in the shed's local time zone at the moment the command is handled.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
loanId LoanId yes The overdue loan. Must be a loan that has been checked out (INV-OVN-10), still open (INV-OVN-5) and overdue today (INV-OVN-6).
neighborId NeighborId yes The borrower, from the list item. Carried onto the event so readers about neighbors match on it directly.
sentTo Text yes The address to send to: the borrower's current email, from the list item's borrowerEmail.
borrowerName Text yes From the list item. Shown in the email.
toolName Text yes From the list item. Shown in the email.
dueDate Date yes From the list item. Must be the loan's current due date (INV-OVN-11). Shown in the email.

Trigger

Triggered by: translation Overdue Notice Gateway, also in this slice, reading Overdue Loans To Notify.

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Overdue Notice Sent → context Loans Read by: Overdue Loans To Notify (the loan leaves the list for good) and My Loans (shows the borrower that a notice was sent).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
loanId LoanId yes From the command. Also the key of the hand-off, which the provider's failure report quotes back.
neighborId NeighborId yes From the command: the borrower.
sentTo Text yes From the command: the address the notice went to.
borrowerName Text yes From the command: the name the notice was addressed to.
toolName Text yes From the command: the tool named in the notice.
dueDate Date yes From the command: the due date the notice gave.
sentAt Instant yes Set by the system: the UTC moment the event is recorded.

The address, name, tool name and due date are facts of the notice: what was actually sent. They are recorded on the event so the hand-off can be repeated, even after a restart, without the list, and so they don't change if the neighbor's details change later. This is the one kind of event that carries copies of names.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. The gateway reads Overdue Loans To Notify, specified in slices/overdue-loans-to-notify.md. Overdue Notice Sent removes the loan from that list and marks the loan on My Loans. Both are eventually consistent: the list may still show a loan for a moment after its notice is recorded, which is why the command itself refuses a second notice.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-OVN-2: At most one overdue notice is sent per loan.
    • Once Overdue Notice Sent is recorded for a loan, the loan is never sent another notice. Notices do not repeat on a schedule.
    • A repeated Send Overdue Notice for a loan whose notice is already recorded succeeds and records nothing, and the gateway hands nothing over for it.
  • INV-OVN-3: Overdue notices go by email only, to the borrower's current email address.
    • Neighbor Registered sets it, Neighbor Email Changed replaces it. The address used is the one recorded on Overdue Notice Sent. An email change after that doesn't resend the notice or change where a pending hand-off goes.
  • INV-OVN-4: Overdue Notice Sent is recorded before the notice is handed to the email provider, and every notice handed over has one.
    • The hand-off is driven from the recorded event and repeated with the same key, after a restart too, until the provider accepts it. That is a technical retry, not a failure of the notice.
    • Overdue Notice Sent doesn't mean the borrower received or read the email. Any failure the provider reports later follows this Overdue Notice Sent.
  • INV-OVN-5: No notice is sent for a loan that has ended, because its tool was returned or recorded lost.
  • INV-OVN-6: The notice goes out as soon as the loan is overdue, with no quiet hours.
    • A loan is overdue from the start of the day after its due date, in the shed's local time. The due date is the latest one set by Tool Checked Out or Loan Extended.
    • A loan that isn't overdue today is refused, for example one extended just before the gateway acted.
  • INV-OVN-7: The notice gives the borrower's name, the tool's name, the due date, a request to return the tool, and that an overdue loan blocks new checkouts and pickups.
    • Its subject line is "Your is overdue".
  • INV-OVN-9: After Overdue Notice Failed, no further notice is attempted for that loan.
    • The loan already has its Overdue Notice Sent, so INV-OVN-2 already stops a second one. The shed manager follows up in person.
  • INV-OVN-10: The loan must exist.
  • INV-OVN-11: The due date given must be the loan's current due date.
    • The gateway reads it from the list, which may be a moment behind. A notice never states a due date the loan no longer has.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ana Ruiz (ana@example.org) borrowed the cordless drill as loan L1, due 12 October, and hasn't returned it. Today is 13 October in the shed's local time.

  • Happy path (INV-OVN-6, INV-OVN-7)
    • Given: at the start of 13 October, shed time, L1 joined Overdue Loans To Notify
    • When: the gateway issues Send Overdue Notice for L1, to ana@example.org, for Ana Ruiz, the cordless drill, due 12 October
    • Then: Overdue Notice Sent is recorded for L1 with that address, name, tool name and due date. The gateway then hands the provider an email to ana@example.org, keyed L1, telling Ana Ruiz the cordless drill was due 12 October, asking her to return it, and saying that an overdue loan blocks new checkouts and pickups.
  • Not overdue on the due date itself (INV-OVN-6)
    • Given: today is 12 October
    • When: a Send Overdue Notice for L1 arrives
    • Then: refused with loan-not-overdue: "This loan isn't overdue." No event is recorded, and nothing is handed over.
  • Extended just before the gateway acted (INV-OVN-11)
    • Given: L1 was on the list, and Loan Extended has just moved its due date to 19 October. The list hasn't caught up yet.
    • When: the gateway issues Send Overdue Notice for L1, giving the due date 12 October
    • Then: refused with due-date-changed: "This loan's due date has changed." No event is recorded, and nothing is handed over.
  • Returned just before the gateway acted (INV-OVN-5)
    • Given: Ana returned the drill, ending L1, and the list hasn't caught up yet
    • When: the gateway issues Send Overdue Notice for L1
    • Then: refused with loan-ended: "This loan has ended." No event is recorded, and nothing is handed over.
  • Recorded lost before the notice (INV-OVN-5)
    • Given: Tool Lost has been recorded for L1
    • When: a Send Overdue Notice for L1 arrives
    • Then: refused with loan-ended. No event is recorded.
  • The gateway reads the same loan twice (INV-OVN-2)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent has been recorded for L1, and the list returned L1 once more before it caught up
    • When: the gateway issues Send Overdue Notice for L1 again
    • Then: the command succeeds and records nothing new. The gateway hands nothing over, so Ana gets one email.
  • No second notice later (INV-OVN-2)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent was recorded for L1, and the drill is still out a week later
    • When: the gateway reads Overdue Loans To Notify
    • Then: L1 isn't on the list, and no further notice is sent.
  • The hand-off call errors (INV-OVN-4)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent has been recorded for L1, and the gateway's first hand-off call to the provider fails with a connection error
    • When: the gateway repeats the hand-off, keyed L1, and the provider accepts it
    • Then: one email goes to ana@example.org. Nothing more is recorded.
  • The process stops before the provider accepts (INV-OVN-4)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent has been recorded for L1, and the process stopped before the hand-off was accepted. L1 has already left Overdue Loans To Notify.
    • When: the gateway starts again
    • Then: it hands the notice over from the recorded Overdue Notice Sent, keyed L1, to ana@example.org with the recorded content. One email goes out.
  • A repeat with different content (INV-OVN-2)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent has been recorded for L1 to ana@example.org
    • When: a Send Overdue Notice for L1 arrives giving ana.ruiz@example.net
    • Then: refused with notice-already-sent: "An overdue notice has already been sent for this loan." No event is recorded, and nothing is handed over.
  • Current email used (INV-OVN-3)
    • Given: Ana changed her email to ana.ruiz@example.net before L1 became overdue
    • When: the gateway issues Send Overdue Notice for L1 with the list's current address
    • Then: Overdue Notice Sent is recorded with sentTo ana.ruiz@example.net, and the email goes there.
  • Email changed after the notice was recorded (INV-OVN-3)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent was recorded for L1 to ana@example.org, and its hand-off hasn't been accepted yet
    • When: Ana changes her email to ana.ruiz@example.net
    • Then: the notice still goes to ana@example.org, the address recorded on it. No second notice is sent.
  • Notice that later fails (INV-OVN-9)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent was recorded for L1, and Overdue Notice Failed was later recorded for it
    • When: the gateway reads Overdue Loans To Notify, and a Send Overdue Notice for L1 arrives anyway
    • Then: L1 isn't on the list. The command succeeds and records nothing new, and nothing is handed over.
  • Unknown loan (INV-OVN-10)
    • Given: no loan L9 has been checked out
    • When: a Send Overdue Notice for L9 arrives
    • Then: refused with loan-not-found: "There is no such loan." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

A refusal records nothing, and the gateway hands nothing over for that loan. No person sees these reasons; they are logged with the loan ID. The name is the contract; the sentence is the log text.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. loan-not-found (INV-OVN-10).
  2. If Overdue Notice Sent is already recorded for the loan: with the same address, name, tool name and due date, the command succeeds and records nothing; otherwise notice-already-sent (INV-OVN-2).
  3. loan-ended (INV-OVN-5).
  4. due-date-changed (INV-OVN-11).
  5. loan-not-overdue (INV-OVN-6).
Reason Sentence Rule
loan-not-found There is no such loan. INV-OVN-10
loan-ended This loan has ended. INV-OVN-5
notice-already-sent An overdue notice has already been sent for this loan. INV-OVN-2
due-date-changed This loan's due date has changed. INV-OVN-11
loan-not-overdue This loan isn't overdue. INV-OVN-6

loan-not-found, loan-ended and due-date-changed mean the same conditions as in Extend Loan. A missing or malformed loan ID (not a UUID), or a blank sentTo, borrowerName or toolName, is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name.

Idempotency: a repeated Send Overdue Notice for a loan that already has its Overdue Notice Sent, with the same content, succeeds and records nothing, and nothing new is handed over. Notices are handed over only from recorded Overdue Notice Sent events.

Hand-off retries: the hand-off is driven from each recorded Overdue Notice Sent until the provider accepts it. A call that errors (the provider unreachable, a timeout), or a stop before acceptance, is repeated with the same key, the loan ID, after a restart too. The provider sends at most one email per key. Delivery attempts after acceptance are the provider's; a final failure is recorded by Record Overdue Notice Failure.

Requests at the same moment: Send Overdue Notice is decided against the loan's events as already recorded, one at a time per loan, so at most one Overdue Notice Sent is recorded for a loan.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: Send Overdue Notice is internal. Only the Overdue Notice Gateway issues it; it is not exposed to neighbors or the shed manager.
  • PII & compliance: the email carries the borrower's name, email address and the tool they have. Overdue Notice Sent records the same, as facts of the notice that was sent. Names and emails are kept with the shed's loan and hold history and never erased.
  • Performance / SLA: the notice is recorded within 5 minutes of the start of the day after the due date (the gateway's read interval), and handed over as soon as the provider accepts it.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool), Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • Overdue Notice Sent (this slice): loanId, sentTo, borrowerName, toolName, dueDate.
    • The gateway reads Overdue Loans To Notify's items: loanId, dueDate, toolName, borrowerName, borrowerEmail (slices/overdue-loans-to-notify.md).
    • These keys match slices/check-out-tool.md and extend-loan.md.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Overdue Loans To Notify (the loan leaves it) and My Loans (shows the notice was sent). Record Overdue Notice Failure matches the provider's failure report to the loan by the hand-off key, the loan ID.

Open Questions

  • Bad input: blank sentTo, borrowerName or toolName is rejected as bad input, not only a malformed loan id (conformance 2026-11-01, finding 6) — v2: stated under Alternate & Error Flows; the subject line is also stated under INV-OVN-7, as for the pickup notice (2026-11-01)

Slice: Record Overdue Notice Failure

Intent

Record that an overdue notice could not be delivered to the borrower, so the shed manager knows the neighbor wasn't told and can follow up in person, and the borrower's My Loans shows that the notice didn't reach them.

Trigger & Actor

Externally triggered. The email provider, outside the shed, sends a final failure report for an overdue notice the shed handed it. The Email Provider Failure Report translation turns that report into the Record Overdue Notice Failure command. No person records a failure, and there is no screen.

What the report carries: the reference the shed gave the notice when it handed it over, which is the loan's ID, since each loan gets at most one overdue notice; and the reason, refused or bounced. Anything else in the report, such as the email address, is not recorded.

Command / Input

Command: Record Overdue Notice Failure

A LoanId is a UUID.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
loanId LoanId yes The reference from the provider's report: the loan the notice was about. Must match an Overdue Notice Sent (INV-ONF-7), for a loan that hasn't ended (INV-ONF-8).
reason Text yes refused or bounced, from the report (INV-ONF-3). Any other value is bad input.

Trigger

Triggered by: translation Email Provider Failure Report, also in this slice (externally triggered by the email provider's final failure report).

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Overdue Notice Failed → context Loans Read by: My Loans (the loan shows the notice couldn't be delivered) and Undelivered Notices (the shed manager's follow-up list).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
loanId LoanId yes From the command.
neighborId NeighborId yes Set by the system: the borrower on the loan's Overdue Notice Sent.
neighborName Text yes Set by the system: the name the notice was addressed to (Overdue Notice Sent.borrowerName).
neighborEmail Text yes Set by the system: the address the notice went to (Overdue Notice Sent.sentTo). Readers that show a current address keep it current themselves.
toolName Text yes Set by the system: the tool the notice named (Overdue Notice Sent.toolName).
dueDate Date yes Set by the system: the due date the notice gave (Overdue Notice Sent.dueDate).
reason Text yes From the command: refused or bounced.
failedAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system. Shown as the failure date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

The event never changes. No later event retries the notice or clears the failure.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Overdue Notice Failed feeds two views, each specified in its own doc:

  • My Loans (slices/my-loans.md) shows the borrower that the overdue notice couldn't be delivered.
  • Undelivered Notices (slices/undelivered-notices.md) lists the failure for the shed manager to follow up.

Both are eventually consistent. Overdue Loans To Notify doesn't hear this event: the loan left that list when Overdue Notice Sent was recorded.

Invariants / Business Rules

Every recorded failure is shown to the shed manager on Undelivered Notices, and to the borrower on My Loans; those views own how it is shown.

A failure is recorded only from the email provider's report; no person records it, and the only way in is the translation in Trigger & Actor. The shed records only the provider's one final failure report: the provider makes 3 delivery attempts over about an hour and reports a final failure only if all of them fail. The shed does no retrying of its own, and a failure a later attempt recovers from is never reported. The provider signs each final report, under the shed's house email-port contract; the translation checks the signature and drops an unsigned or wrongly signed report without issuing any command. The provider's signature, not a sign-in, is what guards this command.

  • INV-ONF-3: Overdue Notice Failed is recorded for the loan the notice was about, with the moment of the failure and whether the email was refused or bounced.
    • Refused and bounced are the two reasons the provider's final report can give.
  • INV-ONF-4: Every Overdue Notice Failed follows an Overdue Notice Sent for the same loan.
    • Overdue Notice Sent is recorded at hand-off, so the loan has already left Overdue Loans To Notify. Recording the failure doesn't change that list.
  • INV-ONF-6: A loan has at most one Overdue Notice Failed. No further notice is attempted for it after a failure.
    • The shed manager follows up in person.
  • INV-ONF-7: A failure report that matches no overdue notice the shed sent is ignored, and nothing is recorded.
  • INV-ONF-8: A failure report that arrives after the loan has ended, because the tool was returned or recorded lost, is ignored, and nothing is recorded.
    • For example, the borrower returned the tool during the hour the provider spent retrying.
  • INV-ONF-9: A failure report repeated for a loan whose failure is already recorded, with the same reason, succeeds and records nothing new. With a different reason it is ignored, and nothing is recorded.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Refused (INV-ONF-3)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent was recorded for Ana's drill loan L1, and the drill is still out
    • When: the provider's final report says the notice for L1 was refused
    • Then: Overdue Notice Failed is recorded for L1, reason refused, with the time it was recorded. No further notice is sent for L1.
  • Bounced (INV-ONF-3)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent was recorded for L1, and the drill is still out
    • When: the provider's final report says the notice for L1 bounced
    • Then: Overdue Notice Failed is recorded for L1, reason bounced.
  • Report matching no notice (INV-ONF-4, INV-ONF-7)
    • Given: no Overdue Notice Sent has been recorded for loan L2
    • When: a failure report names L2
    • Then: ignored with no-matching-notice. Nothing is recorded.
  • Report arrives after the tool was returned (INV-ONF-8)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent was recorded for L1, and Tool Returned was then recorded for L1 while the provider was still retrying
    • When: the provider's final report says the notice for L1 bounced
    • Then: ignored with loan-ended. Nothing is recorded.
  • Report arrives after the tool was recorded lost (INV-ONF-8)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Sent was recorded for L1, and Tool Lost was then recorded for L1
    • When: the provider's final report says the notice for L1 was refused
    • Then: ignored with loan-ended. Nothing is recorded.
  • The same report arrives twice (INV-ONF-6, INV-ONF-9)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Failed was recorded for L1, reason bounced
    • When: the same report, L1 bounced, arrives again
    • Then: it succeeds and nothing new is recorded. L1 still has one Overdue Notice Failed.
  • A second report with a different reason (INV-ONF-6, INV-ONF-9)
    • Given: Overdue Notice Failed was recorded for L1, reason bounced
    • When: a report arrives saying the notice for L1 was refused
    • Then: ignored with failure-already-recorded. Nothing is recorded; L1 keeps its one failure, reason bounced.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: a stable name and a sentence. No person sees these; they go back to the translation, which takes no further action, and are kept for diagnosing the provider link.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. no-matching-notice (INV-ONF-7).
  2. A failure already recorded for the loan (INV-ONF-9): a repeat with the same reason succeeds with nothing recorded; otherwise failure-already-recorded.
  3. loan-ended (INV-ONF-8).
Reason Sentence Rule
no-matching-notice No overdue notice was sent for that loan. INV-ONF-7
failure-already-recorded A failure is already recorded for that notice. INV-ONF-9
loan-ended That loan has already ended. INV-ONF-8

A missing or malformed loan ID, or a reason other than refused or bounced, is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name.

Idempotency: the provider may deliver the same final report more than once. A repeat with the same loan and reason succeeds and records nothing new, even if the loan has since ended. So one failure never shows twice on Undelivered Notices.

Retries and compensations: none in the shed. The provider's own 3 attempts happen before its final report. After a failure no further notice is attempted; following up is the shed manager's job, in person.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the email provider's failure report can trigger this command, through the translation. The provider signs each final report, under the shed's house email-port contract; the translation checks the signature and drops an unsigned or wrongly signed report without issuing any command. The provider's signature, not a sign-in, is what guards this command.
  • PII & compliance: Overdue Notice Failed carries the name and address the notice was sent to, the tool and the date it named, so Undelivered Notices can show the shed manager whom to reach without looking anything up. Nothing else from the provider's report is kept. Names and emails are kept with the shed's loan and hold history and never erased.
  • Performance / SLA: none. A failure shows on Undelivered Notices shortly after the report arrives, about an hour after the notice was handed over.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Overdue Notice Sent (Send Overdue Notice): loanId.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • Overdue Notice Failed (this slice): loanId, reason.
    • Overdue Notice Sent, and the loan's ID as the reference the provider quotes back, match slices/send-overdue-notice.md. Return Tool and Record Tool Lost are specified in slices not yet written in depth; each is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: My Loans and Undelivered Notices (the failure).

Open Questions

None.

Slice: Undelivered Notices

Intent

Shows the shed manager every email the shed couldn't deliver — overdue notices and pickup notices — so they can reach the neighbor another way. A neighbor who wasn't told their loan is overdue, or that a tool is waiting for them, doesn't stay unnoticed. An entry stays only while there is something to follow up.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: the shed manager, opening the Undelivered Notices screen.
  • What it shows: one entry per failed overdue notice whose loan is still open, and one per failed pickup notice whose set-aside hasn't ended, built from the events listed under Read Model / View. The screen offers no actions. Following up is the shed manager's job, in person; no email is tried again after its failure is recorded (Send Overdue Notice, INV-OVN-9).
  • Which failure reports become events is decided by the two failure slices: a report that matches no notice the shed sent, or that arrives after the loan or set-aside has ended, is ignored there and never reaches this view.

Read Model / View

  • View: Undelivered Notices built from events: "Overdue Notice Failed", "Pickup Notice Failed", "Neighbor Email Changed", "Loan Extended", "Tool Returned", "Tool Lost", "Hold Collected", "Hold Cancelled", "Hold Expired"
  • Consumed by: the Undelivered Notices screen (Shed Manager)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual. An entry appears, changes or drops off shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes).

One row per entry. LoanId, HoldId, ToolId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded. A field marked optional can be empty.

Field Type Source / Notes
kind Text overdue-notice or pickup-notice. Derived: from which failure event created the entry.
loanId LoanId Optional; overdue-notice entries only. Overdue Notice Failed.loanId.
holdId HoldId Optional; pickup-notice entries only. Derived: Pickup Notice Failed.holdId.
neighborId NeighborId The failure event's neighborId: the borrower or the holder.
neighborName Text The failure event's neighborName: the name the notice was addressed to.
neighborEmail Text Derived: the failure event's neighborEmail (the address that failed), replaced by each later Neighbor Email Changed.email for that neighbor. Always the current one.
toolId ToolId Optional; pickup-notice entries only. Derived: Pickup Notice Failed.toolId.
toolName Text The failure event's toolName.
dueDate Date Optional; overdue-notice entries only. Overdue Notice Failed.dueDate, replaced by each later Loan Extended.dueDate for the loan.
collectByDate Date Optional; pickup-notice entries only. Derived: Pickup Notice Failed.collectByDate.
reason Text refused or bounced, from the failure event's reason.
failedAt Instant From the failure event's failedAt. Shown as the failure date: its calendar date in the shed's local time zone.

To fill an entry the moment its failure lands, the view also keeps, for every open loan, its tool, borrower and current due date, and for every live set-aside, its tool, holder and collect-by date. These are bookkeeping, not rows, and are never returned.

When an entry drops off.

  • An overdue-notice entry drops off when its loan ends: Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan. Retiring the tool while it is out doesn't end the loan, so the entry stays.
  • A pickup-notice entry drops off when its set-aside ends: Hold Collected, Hold Cancelled or Hold Expired for the hold. Retiring the tool or closing the holder's account ends it by recording Hold Cancelled (Retire Tool, Close Account).

Nothing brings an entry back.

Queries

  • List undelivered notices. Takes nothing. Returns every entry with all the fields above. There is no paging. Entries are listed by neighbor name, then by failedAt, the time the entry was created (INV-UDN-9).

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-UDN-1: Every Overdue Notice Failed and every Pickup Notice Failed creates exactly one entry.
    • Nothing else creates an entry. A failure is recorded only after the email provider has made its 3 delivery attempts over about an hour and reported a final failure, so the shed manager never sees a notice that is still being tried.
  • INV-UDN-2: Each entry shows the failure date, and whether the provider refused the email or it bounced.
    • A bounce usually means a wrong email address. The shed manager can ask the neighbor to change it from My Account.
  • INV-UDN-3: An overdue-notice entry shows the borrower's name and current email, the tool's name, and the loan's current due date.
    • The name, the email, the tool's name and the due date come with Overdue Notice Failed, the email as replaced by any later Neighbor Email Changed and the due date as moved by any later Loan Extended.
  • INV-UDN-3a: A pickup-notice entry shows the holder's name and current email, the tool's name, and the collect-by date.
    • Name, email, tool name and collect-by date come with Pickup Notice Failed; the email is replaced by any later Neighbor Email Changed.
  • INV-UDN-4: An overdue-notice entry drops off when its loan ends: the tool is returned, or the shed manager records it lost.
    • Either way the loan has ended, and there is nothing left to follow up. A tool retired while out keeps its entry until one of these happens.
  • INV-UDN-5: A pickup-notice entry drops off when its set-aside ends.
    • A set-aside ends when the holder collects the tool, or the hold is cancelled or expires; retiring the tool or closing the holder's account records Hold Cancelled for it.
  • INV-UDN-9: Entries are listed by neighbor name, ignoring case, then by when the failure was recorded.
    • The same order as every list in the shed.
  • INV-UDN-8: Applying the same event twice leaves Undelivered Notices as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-UDN-10: Only the shed manager can read Undelivered Notices.
    • A signed-in caller without the shed-manager role is refused with not-shed-manager, and a caller with no sign-in with not-signed-in. Nothing is returned to either.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: Ana Ruiz registered with ana@example.org and has the cordless drill on loan L1, due 12 October. Ben Ito registered with ben@example.org, and Hold Fulfilled was recorded for his hold H1 on the hedge trimmer with a collect-by date of 16 October.

  • Overdue notice fails (INV-UDN-1, INV-UDN-2, INV-UDN-3)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices is empty
    • When: Overdue Notice Failed is recorded for L1 on 13 October, as bounced
    • Then: Undelivered Notices lists an overdue-notice entry: Ana Ruiz, ana@example.org, the cordless drill, due 12 October, failed 13 October, bounced.
  • Due date shown after an extension (INV-UDN-3)
    • Given: Loan Extended moved L1's due date to 19 October, and the loan is now overdue
    • When: Overdue Notice Failed is recorded for L1 on 20 October, as refused
    • Then: the entry shows the due date 19 October, failed 20 October, refused.
  • Pickup notice fails (INV-UDN-1, INV-UDN-2, INV-UDN-3a)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry
    • When: Pickup Notice Failed is recorded for H1 on 13 October, as refused
    • Then: Undelivered Notices also lists a pickup-notice entry: Ben Ito, ben@example.org, the hedge trimmer, collect by 16 October, failed 13 October, refused. Ana's entry is unchanged.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-UDN-8)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry once
    • When: the same Overdue Notice Failed for L1 is applied again
    • Then: the entry is still listed once.
  • Tool returned (INV-UDN-4)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry for L1
    • When: Tool Returned is recorded for L1
    • Then: Ana's entry drops off.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-UDN-4)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry for L1
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for L1
    • Then: Ana's entry drops off.
  • Tool retired while out (INV-UDN-4)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry for L1
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for the cordless drill
    • Then: Ana's entry stays. It drops off once L1 is returned or recorded lost.
  • Holder collects the tool (INV-UDN-5)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry for H1
    • When: Hold Collected is recorded for H1
    • Then: Ben's entry drops off.
  • Someone else checks out the tool (INV-UDN-5)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry for H1, and his collect-by date has passed, but Hold Expired hasn't been recorded
    • When: Cara checks the hedge trimmer out, so Hold Collected is recorded for her hold, not H1
    • Then: Ben's entry stays until Hold Expired is recorded for H1, and then drops off.
  • Holder cancels the hold (INV-UDN-5)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry for H1
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: Ben's entry drops off.
  • Set-aside expires (INV-UDN-5)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry for H1
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for H1
    • Then: Ben's entry drops off.
  • Tool retired while set aside (INV-UDN-5)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry for H1
    • When: Retire Tool records Hold Cancelled for H1, with Tool Retired for the hedge trimmer
    • Then: Ben's entry drops off.
  • Holder closes their account (INV-UDN-5)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry for H1
    • When: Close Account records Hold Cancelled for H1, with Neighbor Account Closed for Ben
    • Then: Ben's entry drops off.
  • Neighbor corrects their email (INV-UDN-3)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry, showing ana@example.org, the address that bounced
    • When: Neighbor Email Changed is recorded for Ana, to ana.ruiz@example.net
    • Then: Ana's entry shows ana.ruiz@example.net. The entry stays until L1 is returned or recorded lost.
  • Listing order (INV-UDN-9)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ben's pickup-notice entry (failed 13 October), Ana's overdue-notice entry (failed 14 October) and Ana's pickup-notice entry (failed 12 October)
    • When: the shed manager lists undelivered notices
    • Then: the entries come back as: Ana's pickup-notice entry, Ana's overdue-notice entry, then Ben's.
  • Listing undelivered notices
    • Given: Undelivered Notices lists Ana's overdue-notice entry and Ben's pickup-notice entry
    • When: the shed manager's screen lists undelivered notices
    • Then: both entries are returned with all their fields, with no paging.
  • A neighbor tries to read the list (INV-UDN-10)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices has entries
    • When: a neighbor, signed in without the shed-manager role, asks for the undelivered notices
    • Then: refused with not-shed-manager: "Only the shed manager can see this screen." Nothing is returned.
  • No sign-in (INV-UDN-10)
    • Given: Undelivered Notices has entries
    • When: a caller with no sign-in asks for the undelivered notices
    • Then: refused with not-signed-in: "Please sign in." Nothing is returned.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Read refusals: the list query refuses a caller without the shed-manager role with not-shed-manager ("Only the shed manager can see this screen."), and a caller with no sign-in with not-signed-in ("Please sign in."). Nothing is returned on a refusal. These mean the same conditions as in the shed manager's commands.
  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-UDN-8). An event applied a second time leaves the entries as they were after the first.
  • Ended loans and set-asides: a failure report for a loan or set-aside that has already ended is ignored by Record Overdue Notice Failure and Record Pickup Notice Failure, so no entry is ever created for one. An entry, once it drops off, never comes back.
  • No actions: the screen issues no commands. Its only use is to prompt the shed manager to follow up in person.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: the Undelivered Notices screen is the shed manager's alone; neighbors never see it. Sign-in, handled outside the shed's events, supplies the shed-manager role; only a caller with it may read this view.
  • PII & compliance: shows neighbors' names, current emails and the tools they have or are waiting for, to the shed manager only. An entry is kept only while its loan or set-aside is live. Names and emails themselves are kept with the shed's loan and hold history and never erased.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Overdue Notice Failed (Record Overdue Notice Failure): loanId, neighborId, neighborName, neighborEmail, toolName, dueDate, reason, failedAt.
    • Pickup Notice Failed (Record Pickup Notice Failure): holdId, toolId, neighborId, neighborName, neighborEmail, toolName, collectByDate, reason, failedAt.
    • Neighbor Email Changed (Change Email): neighborId, email.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool), Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • Hold Collected (Check Out Tool): holdId (the holder collecting ends the set-aside).
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold), Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Cancelled is also recorded by Retire Tool and Close Account, one per hold they end.
    • These keys match the deep-passed docs; the two failure events carrying the notice's details is agreed with slices/record-overdue-notice-failure.md and record-pickup-notice-failure.md.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen issues no commands.

Open Questions

None.
